newsitem.title: USA: Bradley acquires 6 Midwest shopping centers.
newsitem.headline: Bradley acquires 6 Midwest shopping centers.

text.p: Bradley Real Estate Inc said Wednesday it acquired six community shopping centers in Iowa and Illinois for a total price of about $35 million.
Bradley, a real estate investment trust, said it expected to realize a first-year return on the combined properties of about 10.5 percent.

The properties are: Sangamon Center North, a 140,000-square-foot, 97 percent-occupied center in Springfield, Illnois; Fairhills Shopping Center, a 106,000-square-foot, 90 percent-occupied center in Springfield; Parkway Pointe, a 39,000-square-foot, 100 percent-occupied center in Springfield; Holiday Plaza, a 46,000-square-foot, 84 percent-occupied center in Cedar Falls, Iowa; Burlington Plaza, an 89,000-square-foot, 92 percent-occupied center in Burlington, Iowa; and Davenport Retail, a 63,000-square-foot, 100 percent-occupied center in Davenport, Iowa.
All of the centers except the Davenport center were purchased from Lincoln Land Development Co of Springfield, Illinois. The Davenport property was bought from Ryan Development Co of Minneapolis.
Bradley said the transactions were consistent with its strategy of acquiring community shopping centers anchored by grocery stores and located in the Midwest.
The real estate company said its acquisition pipeline was still very active, with numerous transactions in varying stages of negotiation.
Shares of Bradley were unchanged at 19-1/8 early Tuesday afternoon.
